cards.text: Paul, the apostle, is writing to the believers in Rome. He's been talking about his own people, Israel, and how not all of them welcomed the good news. So now he asks it straight out: 'I ask then, did God reject His people?'

cards.question: True or false: Paul answers that yes, God has rejected His people Israel.
Paul says CERTAINLY NOT, then points to himself as an Israelite and a descendant of Abraham. Which tribe is Paul from?

cards.text: If God threw out Israel, He'd have to throw out the guy writing the letter! Paul's holding up his ID like somebody at the door going, 'Check the list. I'm ON it.'
Paul says it again: God did not reject His people, whom He foreknew. Then he brings up Elijah, a prophet of Israel, on one of his roughest days.

cards.question: Paul reminds them what the Scripture says about Elijah: he appealed to God ___ Israel.

cards.text: And Elijah does NOT hold back. He says, 'Lord, they have killed Your prophets and torn down Your altars.'

cards.question: Elijah tells God His prophets are killed and His altars are torn down. Then he tells God who's left. What does Elijah say?

answers.text: He is the only one left

cards.question: True or false: Elijah tells God that the people are seeking his life as well.

cards.text: Friend, I spent years forgotten in the back of a junk drawer, and even I had a twist tie to talk to. Elijah's telling God he's got NOBODY.

cards.question: God replies to Elijah, 'I have reserved for Myself seven thousand men…' What makes those seven thousand stand out?

answers.text: They have not bowed the knee to Baal
They have hidden all of God's prophets
They have rebuilt all of God's altars

cards.question: True or false: God's reply means Elijah was not the only one left who hadn't bowed the knee to Baal.

cards.text: Elijah's flying solo, and God's over here counting SEVEN THOUSAND. That's not you and a buddy, friend, that's a whole ARENA!
Elijah's story wasn't just a trip down memory lane, friend. Paul says God is doing it the same way right now, in his own day.

cards.question: Like the seven thousand in Elijah's day, Paul says there is something at the present time. What is it?
Paul says this remnant is chosen by ___.
True or false: Paul says the remnant is chosen partly by grace and partly by works.

cards.text: Paul says if it's by grace, it's no longer by works, or grace would no longer be grace. Grace you earn isn't a gift, friend, that's a PAYCHECK!
What then? Paul says what Israel was seeking, it failed to obtain.

cards.question: Israel failed to obtain what it was seeking. Who does Paul say did obtain it?
And the rest of Israel? Paul says the others were ___.

cards.text: Paul backs that up with Scripture. It says God gave them a spirit of stupor, to this very day.

cards.question: True or false: The Scripture Paul quotes about a spirit of stupor also says God gave them eyes that could not see and ears that could not hear.

cards.text: Then Paul brings in David, Israel's king, who says, 'May their table become a snare and a trap, a stumbling block and a retribution to them.'

cards.question: David's words go on, and they bring back a picture from the Scripture about a spirit of stupor. Which picture?

cards.text: David finishes, 'May their eyes be darkened so they cannot see, and their backs be bent forever.' Heavy words, friend, so let them sit with you a minute.

findings.problem: The opening card states facts from outside the passage but cites only Romans 11:1. These are that Paul is the apostle writing to the believers in Rome (Romans 1:1, 7) and that not all of Israel welcomed the good news (Romans 10:16).

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing new from the passage. It only reacts with a joke to Romans 11:1, which cards 1 to 3 already covered.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: This story card is a joke-only recap of Romans 11:3, which cards 7 to 9 already covered. It also stretches the text: 'he's got NOBODY' goes beyond Elijah's words, 'I am the only one left.'
This story card is a joke-only recap of Romans 11:4, which cards 11 and 12 already asked about and answered. It doesn't move the passage forward.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: Card 9 cuts the quotation in Romans 11:8 short on purpose. Card 10 then asks whether the missing words ('eyes that could not see, and ears that could not hear') are part of the line. That makes the baker guess the wording of the quoted line instead of reasoning about its meaning.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: Card 11 quotes Romans 11:9, and card 12 asks which picture David's words bring up next. That makes the baker guess the next words of David's quoted line (Romans 11:10).

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The question types in stop 2 follow a strict repeating cycle: multiple choice, fill in the blank, true or false, then the same three again, then multiple choice.

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern.
